subject: chemistry
question_text: Give the formula of borazine. What is its common name?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The formula
lines: The formula of borazine is B₃N₃H₆.
It is a six membered ring of three boron
Each of the six ring atoms carries one
hydrogen, so there are six hydrogens.
steps.why: The formula follows straight from the ring: three boron and three nitrogen atoms alternate around a six membered ring, and each of the six carries one hydrogen.
common_mistakes: Writing B₃N₃H₃. All six ring atoms carry a hydrogen, so the formula is B₃N₃H₆.
Writing BNH₂. That is the empirical formula; the molecule itself is B₃N₃H₆.
steps.memory_tip: Six ring atoms, one hydrogen on each: B₃N₃H₆.
steps.margin_note: Draw the alternating B and N ring if there is room; it fixes the formula.

steps.label: The common name
lines: The common name of borazine is inorganic
The name comes from the likeness to
benzene C₆H₆: both are planar six membered
rings with one hydrogen on each ring atom.
steps.why: One boron and one nitrogen together supply as many electrons as two carbon atoms, so borazine and benzene have the same electron count and the same flat six membered ring — which is where the name inorganic benzene comes from.
common_mistakes: Giving the formula and no name at all. The question asks for the common name as well, so write inorganic benzene or borazole.
Saying it is benzene with boron in it. Borazine is a different compound; only the ring shape and the electron count are like benzene's.
steps.memory_tip: A flat six membered ring like benzene, but built from boron and nitrogen.
steps.margin_note: The question asks two things, so write the formula and the name.

insider_note: Two short answers, the formula B₃N₃H₆ and the name inorganic benzene, and one line on why the name fits completes the page.
